_readme: Splunk field -> target column, per target table, with an evidence level: exact (applied), conditional (applied + flagged with the note), ambiguous (not applied; flagged with candidates). There is no official complete crosswalk; client overrides go in mappings/clients/<client>/field_map.json (see siemx fields import-props). Every column must exist in mappings/fields.json.

ComputerName.note: classic WinEventLog name for the event's <Computer> element

EventCode.note: Splunk's Windows event ID field; SecurityEvent EventID is 'the identifier that the provider used to identify the event'

host.note: Splunk host = the machine that sent the event; equals the source computer only when the forwarder runs on it (not with Windows Event Forwarding collectors)

Account_Name.note: In 4624/4688 'Account Name' appears under Subject (SubjectUserName) and New Logon / Target Subject (TargetUserName).

Account_Domain.note: 'Account Domain' appears under Subject and New Logon.

Security_ID.note: 'Security ID' appears under Subject and New Logon.

Logon_ID.note: 'Logon ID' appears under Subject and New Logon.

user.note: CIM user depends on the event ID and the add-on's props.conf.

src.note: CIM src may be an address or a host name depending on the event.

dest.note: events generated on the target machine (e.g. 4624: 'generates on the computer that was accessed')

xdr_data._note: Windows Event Log records in xdr_data (XDR Collector). Only the fields below are columns; EventData values (TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ...) are inside action_evtlog_data_fields, a JSON string (json_extract_scalar), so they are not mapped by rules. Do not use event_id: it is an internal identifier.

EventCode.note: Windows Event Log records only (event_type 15); the docs say to filter by this field, not event_id

ComputerName.note: the hostname of the source machine

host.note: Splunk host = the machine that sent the event; agent_hostname = the source machine; differs for forwarded events

dest.note: CIM dest for Windows Security = the computer that logged the event

logs-system.security-*._note: Elastic System integration, data stream system.security (Windows Security channel). Raw EventData stays under winlog.event_data.* unless the pipeline moves it to ECS (then it is removed from event_data).

EventCode.note: event.code holds the Windows event ID as a keyword (sample_event.json: event.code = winlog.event_id)

ComputerName.note: the computer that logged the event (Windows Computer element)

host.note: Splunk host = the machine that sent the event; Elastic host.name = the agent's host; they differ for forwarded (WEF) events

dest.note: CIM dest for Windows Security = the computer that logged the event

Source_Network_Address.note: authentication events (Elastic pipeline 'Rename Common Auth Fields': 4624, 4625, 4648, 4768-4771, ...); '-' values are dropped

src_ip.note: authentication events (Elastic pipeline 'Rename Common Auth Fields': 4624, 4625, 4648, 4768-4771, ...); '-' values are dropped

Source_Port.note: authentication events (Elastic pipeline 'Rename Common Auth Fields': 4624, 4625, 4648, 4768-4771, ...); '-' values are dropped; stored as a number

Workstation_Name.note: authentication events (Elastic pipeline 'Rename Common Auth Fields': 4624, 4625, 4648, 4768-4771, ...); '-' values are dropped

Logon_Type.note: raw number kept; winlog.logon.type holds the name instead (3 = Network, 10 = RemoteInteractive)

Logon_Process.note: raw EventData field, not moved by the pipeline

Authentication_Package.note: raw EventData field, not moved by the pipeline

Process_Name.note: events with a ProcessName field (authentication events); full path

New_Process_Name.note: event 4688 only (Elastic pipeline 'Process Event 4688'); full path

New_Process_ID.note: event 4688 only (Elastic pipeline 'Process Event 4688'); Elastic stores a number (0x1a2 -> 418), Windows shows hex

Process_Command_Line.note: event 4688 only (Elastic pipeline 'Process Event 4688'); needs command-line auditing enabled

Token_Elevation_Type.note: raw EventData value (%%1936 / %%1937 / %%1938); Splunk classic logs show 'TokenElevationTypeFull (2)': rewrite values; verify

Mandatory_Label.note: raw EventData field, not moved by the pipeline

Account_Name.note: subject or target account; Elastic fills user.name from SubjectUserName or TargetUserName depending on the event code

user.note: subject or target account, depends on the event code

Account_Domain.note: subject or target domain, depends on the event code

Security_ID.note: subject or target SID, depends on the event code

Logon_ID.note: winlog.logon.id is copied from TargetLogonId or SubjectLogonId depending on the event

logs-system.security-*._types: type = the ECS field type (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/ecs): source.ip ip, source.port long, process.pid long; Kibana KQL wildcards fail on non-string types
